archetypes.name: parity
archetypes.rationale: Bash-to-Python port must preserve exact behavioral parity; the static correctness reviewer lacks the deleted bash code context needed for comparison.
archetypes.prompt_body: This diff ports several bash helpers to Python CLI verbs. Compare `python/blocker.py` and `python/issue_query.py` against the deleted bash scripts for behavioral divergences. Focus on: (1) `parse_prose_blockers` regex parity with the old `sed` pipeline — especially per-line backtick-stripping, emphasis-stripping, cross-line non-match, and the `Depends on [#150](url)` vs `[Depends on #150](url)` markdown-link asymmetry; (2) `issue state` validation matrix — flag-looking value rejection for `--issue`/`--repo`, non-numeric `--issue`, missing `--issue` — and whether exact error message text matches the bash predecessor; (3) `issue info` fail-open vs fail-closed boundaries, especially the missing-value-exit-1-no-VALUE= contract (matching `${2:?...}` under `set -euo pipefail`); (4) `issue context` exit code matrix (exit 2 for validation/missing-args, exit 1 for runtime, no KV envelope on non-zero); and (5) `IS_PR` lowercase boolean emission vs Python's `True`/`False`. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: output-routing
archetypes.rationale: The quiet-init + emit_kv routing contract is load-bearing for shell consumers; any bare print() after quiet_init silently empties the KV block the caller parses.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit the quiet-mode KV output routing in the four new main functions across `python/blocker.py` and `python/issue_query.py`. After `logging_util.quiet_init(...)` is called, stdout is redirected to the quiet log; all contract KV (BLOCKERS=, STATE=, URL=, IS_PR=, VALUE=, TITLE_FILE=, BODY_FILE=, FAILED=, ERROR=) must flow through `logging_util.emit_kv`, never via bare `print()` or `sys.stdout.write()`. Specifically check whether `issue_context_main`'s `--help` path calls `print(_usage())` after `quiet_init` has already redirected stdout, and whether that usage text therefore goes to the quiet log instead of the terminal. Also verify that the shell adapter in `scripts/implement-admission.sh` correctly captures KV from the Python subprocess via command substitution given that `emit_kv` writes to FD 3, not FD 1, and trace whether the awk extraction line can handle a BLOCKERS= value that contains spaces. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: harness-integration
archetypes.rationale: Multiple shell test harnesses were updated to intercept new Python CLI verbs; missed dispatch arms or wrong KV formats silently break offline test coverage.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the changes to `scripts/test-implement-admission.sh`, `skills/implement/scripts/test-implement-bootstrap.sh`, and `scripts/test-implement-finalize.sh` to verify that every updated stub dispatcher correctly intercepts `python3 ... cli.py blocker all-open`, `cli.py issue state`, `cli.py issue context`, and `cli.py issue info`. Check that stubs emit KV in exactly the format the new Python code produces — particularly that IS_PR is lowercase `true`/`false`, that FAILED= and ERROR= are emitted as two separate lines, and that BLOCKERS= is emitted for the no-blocker case. Verify that `make_python3_stub` in the admission harness intercepts invocations where the path to `cli.py` is absolute (not just a bare relative name), and that the Makefile shard assignments include both `test-blocker` and `test-issue-query` without inadvertently dropping any existing retired targets. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
